# HAProxy — load-balancer

Two backends balanced round-robin with sticky sessions via a ROUTEID cookie that HAProxy inserts itself, so the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME distinguishes which one served the page.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/http/load-balancer/vaadin.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# Two backends behind one frontend, with sticky sessions.
#
# Vaadin needs affinity: the session lives in one backend's memory, so a request
# that lands on the other one finds no UI. HAProxy synthesizes its own affinity
# cookie rather than reading a route id out of JSESSIONID, so — as in every
# other tree here — the backends need no Tomcat jvmRoute. APP_NAME is what
# distinguishes them in the rendered page.
#
# See load-balancer-cookie-prefix for the other idiom, where HAProxy rewrites
# the session cookie in flight instead of adding one of its own.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    bind :80
    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    balance roundrobin

    # `insert` adds the cookie, `indirect` keeps it out of the request the
    # backend sees, `nocache` stops a shared cache storing a response that
    # carries one. The first request has no cookie and is balanced normally,
    # which is why CI warms both backends before the tests: a cold JVM
    # answering a browser's first render can exceed the test timeout.
    cookie ROUTEID insert indirect nocache httponly

    server vaadin-1 vaadin-1:8080 cookie v1
    server vaadin-2 vaadin-2:8080 cookie v2
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
